cards.note: External plugin already on the single official profile-bundle path: dsh.bundle.patch, installed by 'dsh plugin --profile probe add .'; no repository-plugins row or .dsh-plugin artifact; peer floor rewritten to the target cohort (rollup R-08 #3) and verified by a scratch-profile install plus cold boot.
No Web Client half and no legacy dshClient field or dsh.plugin.json in the manifest.
No client bundle is built or mounted, so there is no dsh.client declaration for the client-modules scan.
inject = [] and apply() touches only ctx.effect; no ctx.get or property service access needs declaring.
No optional host service is probed or read, so there is nothing to switch to a weak ctx.get.
No session/event subscription and no session-state derivation from event fields.
Not a self-rendering client: no client half, no ctx.sessions consumption, no /state route.
No tasks/jobs output tailing, so tasks.peek has no call site.
Injects and calls none of httpServer/tasks and registers no onTaskDone listener (inject = []).
No ImageAttachmentRef use, read_image output, or image metadata persisted by the plugin.
read_image is neither registered, wrapped, parsed, nor snapshot-tested here.
No DeepSeek LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache in the plugin.
Ordinary Cordis server-side plugin; no APIProxy call site and no ctx.remote use.
The target is alpha.2, not alpha.1, so this card's condition is not met; the corridor net state is read from A2-01, and this plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents anyway.
No host-source patch (the repository ships no patches/ directory) and no import from internal session-view paths.
Ships a bundle patch layer but reads no profile files and hardcodes no DSH_HOME; verification uses the official launcher and a scratch profile.
Not a headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser; its load marker is written to stderr, the diagnostic channel the card preserves.
No tool-presentation mode, PTC preset, dispatch waterfall, or related type use.
No permission/approval/WebFetch policy in the plugin or its patch layer, so the changed default has no local confirmation step to preserve or add.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route, browser page, or /api handler to gate.
Not a model-provider plugin; optional capability with no local workaround to retire.
No UI, localization resources, or custom i18n patch.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model selector.
Informational deployment-level privacy default; the plugin carries no adapter code and no user-facing disclosure.
No persistent PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker workaround exists to delete.
No session-log-deepseek upload logic or configuration; the plugin makes no log egress decision.
No browser acceptance script or wrapper in the repository; the documented check is a headless boot, not a __DSH_BOOT__ read.
No userQuestions answerer registration and no TUI-style question handling.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions and no agent-presets roots configuration.
No isTokenDelta use or TPS computation.
The layer sits on dsh-base but inserts only its own row; it states no telemetry privacy stance and overrides no telemetry or plugin-inventory row.
No @earendil-works/pi-ai import, provider directory, or credential/auth code.
No @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime import and no dsh.client.inject declaration.
No Web Client bundle or assembly row, so the entry/module/registration id rule has nothing to align.
No session-timeline or user-message content read; the plugin has no client half.
No composer DOM manipulation, draft injection, or history recall.
No MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock rendering from ui-primitives.
No ctx.connection.api consumption and no history/transcript read.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptor construction and no subagent/descriptor assertion.
No ctx.workspaces navigation calls and no workspaces.list snapshot reads.
No third-party persisted SessionEvents are produced and no persistence/reload/transport layer is owned.
No ctx.remote call and no Remote failure branch to move onto RemoteError.

Dependency graph reviewed: the dsh-agent peer is the fixture's documented host-compatibility declaration, not an override kept for a pruned peer, so it stays and no dependency is trimmed; alpha.2's added peer is handled by A2-08. No lockfile exists to change.
No startup wrapper, CI matrix, or Node-version workaround (forcing Node 22, skipping dsh web) exists in this repository.
No pluginInventory/list consumer and no PluginInventorySnapshot validation.
No client Remote use and no need for the Host home/loopback facts.
